question: In a pure capacitor connected to an AC source, how will the capacitive reactance change if the frequency of the source is doubled? Justify your answer.

options.A: The capacitive reactance becomes double because $X_C\propto f$.
options.B: The capacitive reactance remains unchanged because capacitance is unchanged.
options.C: The capacitive reactance becomes half because $X_C=\dfrac{1}{2\pi fC}$ and $f'=2f$.
options.D: The capacitive reactance becomes one-fourth because frequency doubles.
